title: Selvage Session Protocol — every method
description: The two client-to-server methods, with the params each takes and the result each returns. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §5. The mapping is: `session.hello` → `sessionHelloParams` and no response frame at all (its result is the `room.created`/`room.joined` event); `session.rename` → `renameParams`, result `{}`. An unknown method is answered with an error response and never dropped.

anyMethod.description: A method name: one of the two above, an `x.`-prefixed reserved name (§10.1), or any other string at all. A name the server does not implement is answered with `unknown_method`; it is not a malformed frame.

knownMethod.description: The method names this protocol defines.

anyParams.description: Method-specific params. Absent is equivalent to `{}`, and for a method that requires a member both are answered `bad_params`. Params are not `null`: an explicit `null` is a malformed frame (CANONICAL.md §2.6).

awareness_client_id.description: The awareness client id this connection will speak with. Omitted means this connection publishes no awareness, and the server then omits `awareness_client_id` from its `PeerInfo`.

capabilities.description: What the client believes it has. The server ignores any it does not know.

client.description: Free-form client identification, for diagnostics only.

anyResult.description: Every result this protocol has: `{}`, because neither method returns anything. What a caller used to read back from a reply — the room's listing, the set of paths open — is the host's sealed state and a peer's sealed holds, which arrive over the relay and are verified rather than answered (`PROTOCOL.md` §7.1, §13.7).
